text:
emma: Quick check — when we onboarded ranker-v3 on the new dataset, goldset-only eval showed +1.8% NDCG@10 vs baseline but synthetic-augmented eval shows -0.6%. Anyone else seeing mismatch? :thinking:
raj: I ran the same eval. Goldset = curated human judgments (n=8k). Synthetic = auto-sampled negatives from BM25 (n=50k). Differences in candidate pool size could explain.
liam: Could be candidate pool leak — are we deduping between train and goldset? I saw duplicates in synthetic cands.
sara: @liam yes we found ~1.2% overlap when we used `--candidate-source=all`. Fixing to `--dedupe=true` changed NDCG by ~0.4.
emma: Also noticed synthetic negatives were top-heavy — the sampled BM25 negatives are too easy. That inflates MRR in synthetic eval for older models.
raj: Proposed experiment: create two synthetic splits — hard negatives (cross-encoder topK) vs easy (bm25). Compare ndcg/mrr across both.
niko: ran a quick A/B: hard-neg synthetic -> NDCG down by 0.9 vs gold; easy-neg -> NDCG up 0.3. Seems model exploits easy negatives.
sara: Could quantization be amplifying this? We're evaluating 4bit PTQ for bringup.
liam: Quantized v3-int4 showed MRR drop mostly on hard-neg slices. Int8 had much smaller delta.
emma: actionable: 1) add hard-neg synthetic to validation, 2) record slice-wise ndcg/mrr (by query length, doc length, domain), 3) dedupe candidate pools.
raj: also add `eval_bias_check` metric: ndcg_ratio = ndcg(hard)/ndcg(easy) to detect exploitation.
sara: quick command I ran:
```
python eval.py --model candidate-v3-int4 --goldset goldset.json --synthetic-hard synth_hard.json --slices slices.yaml --out reports/v3-int4.json
```
liam: let's add a dashboard card in Redwood Console (model->v3->slices) for hard/easy comparison.
emma: thanks — I'll roll this into the onboarding checklist for next model bringups. cc @sara @raj :thumbsup:
eval-bot: Results pushed to s3://redwood-evals/1708304321-v3-int4-report.json :rocket:
